idea: I run a small independent pharmacy and want a tool that reminds patients when their repeat prescriptions are due for refill. I am the only pharmacist; my technician handles pickup. Getting a reminder wrong could mean a missed medication, so I would rather send no reminder than a wrong one.

problem: Patients forget refills and lapse on medication; today I notice only when they come in late and flustered.
user: I am the operator; my technician marks pickups. Patients only receive messages, they never log in.
workflow: When I dispense a repeat, the tool schedules a reminder a few days before the refill date; the technician marks it done at pickup.
success: Fewer lapsed repeats: if late pickups drop noticeably within two months, it works.
safety: A wrong dosage or wrong-patient reminder is the nightmare case. Reminders must never state dosage, only that a refill is due, and an unclear record must produce no reminder at all.
data: Names, phone numbers, and medication names are sensitive. Everything stays on the pharmacy computer; no cloud.
non-goals: No online ordering, no payments, no chat with patients in the first version.
